expect_nodes.name: orders
expect_nodes.note: publisher.topic_path('my-project', 'orders') then publisher.publish(topic_path, data) -- the topic is arg #1 of topic_path(, never of publish(

expect_nodes.name: orders-worker
expect_nodes.note: subscriber.subscription_path('my-project', 'orders-worker') -- the subscriber names a SUBSCRIPTION, not the topic

expect_edges.note: the subscription-to-topic binding lives in IaC, not code (A2.6 caveat), so this edge is not provable from source alone today; it is kept as the intended graph so a real binding resolver has a gate, and so a name-equality pairing cannot score it

forbid.name: event_emit:publish
forbid.note: MEASURED VIOLATION: the generic `publish(` needle finds no literal in publisher.publish(topic_path, ...) and names the event after the METHOD -- an identity-free node any other `.publish(var)` call would share

forbid.name: event_handle:subscribe
forbid.note: MEASURED VIOLATION: the same for subscriber.subscribe(subscription_path, ...)

note: A15.7 baseline 2026-09-17: NONE via=eventbus -- no queue node; the only nodes are two method-named event phantoms. The subscription is deliberately NOT named after the topic: in production it rarely is. Keyed on QUEUE_* + QUEUE_FLOWS for every messaging cell in A15.7, including the eventbus-first mechanisms, because that is the graph A2.6 (cloud brokers) and A2.9 (MQTT / Redis pub/sub / NATS leave eventbus.rs) are building: an EVENT_* key would read `none` the moment those fixes land. `via` still records the eventbus path when it is the one that fired.
